newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo must get chance for reforms success - minister.
newsitem.headline: Yugo must get chance for reforms success - minister.

text.p: Yugoslavia must be given a chance to return to world markets and begin earning money if its pledged reforms are to succeed, Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic said.
"The problem is we are in a vicious circle at this moment and what we expect, hope and ask for is a chance to equally participate in market competition," Djunic told Reuters in an interview.
Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, is still barred access to world trade and financial organisations although the war-related U.N. embargo against the country was lifted in October 1996.

To get the ban lifted, Belgrade must cooperate with a war crimes tribunal in The Hague, improve human rights in Serbia's mostly-Albanian province of Kosovo and make progress in talks with other ex-Yugoslav republics on division of the former federation's assets.
So far Belgrade has failed to comply with any of these conditions but officials are pressing for the lifting of the U.S.-imposed outer wall of sanctions.
"To return to world organisations, we must carry out adequate reforms, but we cannot carry out reforms without money, and we have no money because we have no access to world markets," Djunic said.
In that context, it is very important for Yugoslavia to be given a chance to export, to get trade preferentials for western Europe and access to international funding, he said.

"The effects of all that will be reinvested to support the entire process of economic reforms which will in the end inevitably and certainly lead to all other reforms that are expected of us," Djunic said.

"We are prepared to join the market under equal conditions, but we must be given opportunities, and if we are, we will make use of them by substantially speeding up reforms, privatisation and restructuring of the economy and banking sector through the business effects achieved," Djunic said.
Large industrial systems still cannot part company with their "social employment function" and lay off thousands of unnecessary workers without concrete social programmes.
"We do not have the funds to pay for that and we cannot find the funds if we cannot export our goods," Djunic said.
Yugoslavia wants to create conditions for foreign partners who want to work in market conditions amid normal competition, Djunic said.
"We invite foreign partners to come and earn money for themselves and in the process also help us earn something, employ our people and raise GDP," Djunic said.

"I appeal and expect the sequence of moves to be slightly altered and to be, what we feel, more logical," Djunic said, adding that more emphasis must be given to economic recovery. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
